what: Block runs two businesses. Square sells payment hardware and software to small businesses, and Cash App is a consumer money app used for payments, direct deposit, stock and bitcoin buying. It also owns Afterpay, a buy-now-pay-later service.
customers: Small and medium businesses using Square, and consumers using Cash App, mostly in the United States.
money: transaction fees, Cash App Card interchange, bitcoin sales and lending
payment processing, hardware and software subscriptions for merchants
moat: Two networks that feed each other: consumers paying businesses that already use Square, with services that are hard to unpick once a small business runs its till, payroll and loans through one system.
risks: Cash App user growth has slowed
Bitcoin trading revenue is large but carries almost no margin
Consumer lending exposes it to credit losses
opportunities: Analysts see about 30% upside from current levels
Cash App is being built into a full banking relationship with direct deposit and lending
Cash of about $8 billion exceeds its debt
watch: Gross profit growth at Cash App and Square separately, and monthly active Cash App users.
